## Authentication

Every request needs **two** things: the token, which says which **organization** you are, and the `X-Workspace-Id` header, which says which of its **workspaces** to act on.

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Workspace-Id: <workspace uuid>
```

### The token

A Bearer JWT signed **RS256** by the Kobana authorization server (HS512 only against a local development server).

| Claim | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`org`** | **The tenant.** The organization's `public_id` — what decides which data the token reaches. |
| `sub` | The **person** who consented. It picks no data, but caps what the token does at their permissions in the organization (see below). |
| `scope` | Space-separated list (e.g. `finance.payables finance.people.write`). A `.write` scope also grants read. |
| `jti` | Token identifier, used for revocation. |
| `iss` / `aud` / `exp` | Issuer, audience and expiry. |

⚠️ The tenant is `org`, never `sub`. They are different identifier spaces: a person id never matches an organization, so a token built from the wrong one fails on every request.

### The person's permissions

The scope is the **application's** ceiling, decided at consent. When `sub` is a person who has signed in to Finance, the API also requires from them the **same permission** the action needs in the dashboard: a `finance.payables.write` token belonging to someone who may only list payables cannot create one. Suspended, pending or removed members reach nothing, and the person must have access to the `X-Workspace-Id` workspace. A token whose `sub` is not a member of the organization (a system token) stays capped by its scopes only.

### The `X-Workspace-Id` header

An organization can own **several workspaces**, and every route in this API answers for exactly **one**. The token alone does not say which — which is why the header is required on every operation.

It is a **selector, never a grant**: the workspace you name is checked against the token's organization. A workspace owned by another organization answers exactly like one that does not exist — deliberately, so the response never reveals that the id is real somewhere else.

| Situation | Response |
| :--- | :--- |
| Header absent | `400` `WORKSPACE_REQUIRED` |
| Workspace of another organization, nonexistent, or malformed id | `403` `UNKNOWN_WORKSPACE` |
| `org` matches no organization | `403` `UNKNOWN_ORGANIZATION` |
| Scope insufficient for the operation | `403` `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` |
| A workspace Security rule blocked the operation (`details.reason` says which) | `403` `SECURITY_BLOCKED` |
| The token's person lacks the permission the operation requires (`details.required` says which) | `403` `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSION` |
| The token's person is suspended, pending, removed or holds no permission in the organization | `403` `MEMBERSHIP_INACTIVE` |
| The token's person has no access to this workspace | `403` `WORKSPACE_ACCESS_DENIED` |

### Example

```bash
curl https://api.finance.kobana.com.br/v1/payables \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOBANA_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Workspace-Id: $KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID"
```

For command-line testing, export both: `export KOBANA_TOKEN=xxxxxxxx` and `export KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID=xxxxxxxx`, then paste the commands from the docs straight into your terminal.

## Format

The API accepts `JSON` only. Every request must use `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response uses `snake_case`.

| Field Type | Format |
| :--- | :--- |
| **DateTime** | [ISO8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format. Examples — Date: `2026-01-24`. Date and time: `2026-01-24T10:07:00.000Z` |
| **Money** | Decimal as a string with 2 places (`"150.00"`). Always positive — the direction is given by the `type` field (`debit`/`credit`) or by context (payable/receivable). |
| **UUID** | Resource identifiers in UUID v4 format |

## Conventions

Conventions used throughout this documentation:

| Convention | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`:id`** | Path parameter to be replaced with the resource's UUID. |
| **`#{variable}`** | A value from your account to be substituted in the example. |
| **`...`** | Response content truncated for readability. |
| **`$KOBANA_TOKEN`** | JWT access token. Export it with `export KOBANA_TOKEN=xxxxxxxx`. |
| **`$KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID`** | Workspace UUID, sent in `X-Workspace-Id`. Export it with `export KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID=xxxxxxxx`. |

## Status Codes

The API returns standard HTTP status codes:

| | Code | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ✅ | **200 OK** | Successful request with a response body. |
| ✅ | **201 Created** | Resource created successfully. |
| ✅ | **204 No Content** | Successful request with no response body. |
| ❌ | **400 Bad Request** | Invalid request — malformed body, filter not allowed, or `X-Workspace-Id` missing. |
| ❌ | **401 Unauthorized** | Missing, invalid, or expired token. |
| ❌ | **403 Forbidden** | Insufficient scope or permission, unknown organization, or a workspace outside it. |
| ❌ | **404 Not Found** | Resource not found or outside the workspace. |
| ❌ | **422 Unprocessable Entity** | Valid request, but the submitted data is not. |
| ❌ | **429 Too Many Requests** | Rate limit reached. |
| ❌ | **500 Internal Server Error** | Internal processing error. Check the [server status](https://status.kobana.com.br). |

## Listing and Pagination

Every listing endpoint uses **cursor-based pagination**:

```
GET /v1/payables?cursor=<opaque_cursor>&limit=25
```

The response includes `meta.next_cursor` — pass it as `?cursor=` on the next request to fetch the following page. When `meta.next_cursor` is `null`, there are no more pages.

## Idempotency

Creation operations (`POST`) accept the `X-Idempotency-Key` header. Retries with the same key return the original result without creating duplicates — safe to retry on network failure.

```
X-Idempotency-Key: <client-generated-uuid-v4>
```

## Request ID

Every request has an associated identifier, available in the `Request-Id` response header. This value helps with debugging and auditing. The request log is kept for **30 days**. When opening a support ticket about a specific request, provide the `Request-Id` to speed up the investigation.

## Security

The API uses **2048-bit SSL** certificates. Every request must go over **HTTPS** — calls to port 80 are redirected to 443.

Clients must support `TLSv1.2` or `TLSv1.3` with one of the following ciphers: `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`, `ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384`. `TLSv1` and `TLSv1.1` are not supported.

## HTTP Cache

Use HTTP cache headers to reduce load and gain speed. Most responses include `ETag` and/or `Last-Modified` — store these values and send them back on subsequent requests via `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`. If the resource has not changed, the response is `304 Not Modified`, with no body and no reprocessing.

## Error Handling

5xx errors indicate server failures: **500 Internal Server Error** (application unavailable), **502 Bad Gateway**, **503 Service Unavailable**, and **504 Gateway Timeout** (transient infrastructure failures). Your application should detect these codes and reschedule the request after a few minutes with exponential backoff. Server status: [https://status.kobana.com.br](https://status.kobana.com.br).
